components.title: What is ReAct?
components.definition: ReAct (Reasoning and Acting) is a large language model prompting paradigm proposed by Princeton University and Google. It requires the model to alternate between generating Reasoning Traces and Specific Actions when solving complex problems. This approach allows the model not only to make decisions but also to observe the results of its actions (Observation), thereby dynamically adjusting subsequent thinking and planning.
components.example:
Question: What is the elevation range for the area that the eastern sector of the Colorado plateau goes up into?

Thought 1: I need to search Colorado plateau, find its eastern sector, then find the elevation range of the area it goes up into.
Action 1: Search[Colorado plateau]
Observation 1: The Colorado Plateau... is centered on the Four Corners region... 
Thought 2: It does not mention the eastern sector. Let me look up the eastern sector...

questions.question: In the standard ReAct execution loop, what step immediately follows an Action?
options: Observe the results returned by the environment (Observation)
Reflect on whether the previous action was correct (Reflexion)
questions.explanation:
Analysis:
The standard ReAct loop is Thought -> Action -> Observation. After executing an action, the model must wait and observe the results returned by the environment before proceeding to the next round of Thought based on those results.
